parts.visual:
A team spends 8 months in a conference room designing a 'smart coffee cup' with a bluetooth thermometer. They launch it. Nobody buys it. Why? Because they never actually talked to a person who drinks coffee. They assumed the user's problem was temperature; the real problem was time.

The Interview:
1. The Illusion of Knowledge: Sitting in an office looking at analytics dashboards is a trap. Data tells you 'what' users are doing. Only talking directly to users tells you 'why' they are doing it.
2. Radical Empathy: A PM's superpower is setting aside their own ego and deeply listening to the pain, frustrations, and actual workflows of the customer without interrupting or selling to them.
parts.audio: Users lie. They don't mean to, but they do. If you ask a user 'Would you use this feature?', they will say yes just to be polite. The art of the user interview is never asking about the future; you must only ask them about their actual behavior in the past.

questions.question: What is the 'Mom Test' in user interviews?
options: A framework for asking questions that even your mom can't lie to you about. Instead of asking 'Is this a good idea?' (which invites a polite lie), you ask 'Talk me through the last time you tried to solve this problem.' You focus on past facts, not future opinions.
questions.correct_answer: A framework for asking questions that even your mom can't lie to you about. Instead of asking 'Is this a good idea?' (which invites a polite lie), you ask 'Talk me through the last time you tried to solve this problem.' You focus on past facts, not future opinions.
questions.explanation: Past behavior is the only reliable predictor of future action.

questions.question: Listen to the PM conducting an interview. Why did they interrupt the user?
questions.tts_text: User: 'I think I would probably use a calendar integration if you built it.' PM: 'Wait, let's go back. Last week, when you scheduled a meeting, what exact tool did you physically open first?'
options: Anchoring to Reality. The user was guessing about their future desires. The PM interrupted to force the user to describe a concrete, historical action. People are terrible at predicting their future desires, but excellent at remembering their past pain.
questions.correct_answer: Anchoring to Reality. The user was guessing about their future desires. The PM interrupted to force the user to describe a concrete, historical action. People are terrible at predicting their future desires, but excellent at remembering their past pain.
questions.explanation: Don't ask them what they want. Ask them what they did.

questions.question: Why is it dangerous to 'Pitch' your product during a user interview?
options: It biases the data. If you spend 10 minutes explaining why your idea is brilliant, the user will feel pressured to agree with you to avoid awkwardness. A PM must remain entirely neutral and act like a curious investigator, not a salesperson.
Because the user might steal it.
questions.correct_answer: It biases the data. If you spend 10 minutes explaining why your idea is brilliant, the user will feel pressured to agree with you to avoid awkwardness. A PM must remain entirely neutral and act like a curious investigator, not a salesperson.
questions.explanation: You are there to learn, not to convince.

questions.question: What does 'Observing the Workaround' mean?
options: Finding gold. If you watch a user use 3 different Excel spreadsheets, a sticky note, and a calculator just to generate one report, you have found a massive point of friction. The 'workaround' proves the problem is severe enough that they will pay you to fix it.
questions.correct_answer: Finding gold. If you watch a user use 3 different Excel spreadsheets, a sticky note, and a calculator just to generate one report, you have found a massive point of friction. The 'workaround' proves the problem is severe enough that they will pay you to fix it.
questions.explanation: Ugly workarounds are the blueprints for billion-dollar products.

The terrible mistake of trying to sell your idea during a research interview
A painful, manual process the user created, proving a deep need for a solution
Deeply understanding the user's frustration without imposing your own ego
